Information entropy minimization captures how organisms reduce uncertainty through sensory input and motor output. Feedback loop adjustment formalizes the closed-loop nature of perception-action cycles, where actions modify the environment and feed back into perception. Communication as adjustment extends this to intersubjective processes, where shared information enables coordinated environmental modification. These primitives form a coherent framework for modeling intelligence as adaptive information processing, with entropy as a measure of adjustment efficiency and feedback as a mechanism for iterative refinement. The failure modes include sensory overload, delayed feedback, and channel saturation, each leading to suboptimal adjustment strategies.
